title: Assay for quantitative determination of CYP1A1 enzyme activity using 7-Ethoxyresorufin as standard substrate \(EROD assay)
protocol: Supplement DMEM with 1 mM sodium pyruvate.
Add 4 mM L-glutamine to the supplemented DMEM.
Include 10% FBS in the supplemented DMEM.
Add 100 U/ml penicillin to the supplemented DMEM.
Mix 100 μg/ml streptomycin into the supplemented DMEM.
Adjust Cell EROD reaction buffer pH to 8.0 with NaH2PO4.
Prepare TE-enzymatic microsome buffer at pH 7.4 with 1 mM EDTA.
Create cell stop reaction solution using fluorescamine in acetonitrile (150 μg/ml).
Mix resorufin stock solution in DMSO (2 mM) just before use.
Pre-warm buffers and media at 37°C before contact with growing cells.
Grow cells in a flask using DMEM and standard growth conditions.
Trypsinize cells from prepared flasks when they are approximately 80% confluent.
Count cell concentration using a coulter counter or hemocytometer.
Plate 200 µl of diluted cells (1 x 10^4 cells) to each well of a 96-well plate.
Incubate plates at 5% CO2, 37°C, and 95% humidity.
Start treating the cells once they reach 100% confluency.
Remove the medium after exposure time and rinse with 200 µl of PBS.
Add 100 µl of 2µM EROD solution to each well immediately.
Incubate for 20 minutes.
Stop the treatment by adding 75 µl of fluorescamine solution in acetonitrile (150 µg/ml) to each well.
Prepare a calibration curve in the range of 0 to 50 pmol of resorufin using the resorufin calibration standard.
Measure fluorescence at an excitation wavelength of 535 nm and emission wavelength of 590 nm.
Collect tissue samples.
Immediately freeze collected tissue samples in liquid nitrogen and store at −80 °C until required for microsome preparations.
Homogenize frozen tissue (2.5 mg) with ice-cold 10 mM Tris-HCl buffer (5 mL) containing 250 mM sucrose at pH 7.4.
Centrifuge the homogenized tissue at 10000 × g for 10 min at 4 ºC.
Remove the pellet and add calcium chloride (8 mM) to the supernatant, mix well, and allow standing at 4 ºC for 4 min.
Centrifuge the supernatants at 25000 × g for 30 min at 4 ºC to separate the microsomal and cytosolic fractions.
Resuspend the microsomal fraction in 50 mM Tris-HCl containing 0.1 mM EDTA and 20% glycerol at pH 7.4.
Determine the microsomal protein concentrations with a commercially available kit (Bio-Rad laboratories Inc., Hercules, CA, USA).
Store prepared microsomes at -80 ºC until required for assay.
Dissect gill arches and place them in HEPES-Cortland (HC) buffer.
For rainbow trout, use 2-mm pieces cut from the tip of gill filaments, while whole gill arches are used for zebrafish.
Transfer duplicate groups of 10 filaments per fish for trout assay and for zebrafish assay one whole gill arch per fish into two wells containing HC buffer using a pasteur pipet.
Replace the HC buffer in the plate with 0.5 ml of reaction buffer.
Incubate the plate with continuous shaking, covered with aluminium foil to prevent degradation of 7-ethoxyresorufin.
Following 10 min of preincubation at room temperature, replace buffer with 0.7 ml of fresh reaction buffer and incubate again.
After the incubation period, transfer 0.2 ml aliquots from each well to a 96-well plate.
Measure fluorescence at excitation wavelength of 535 nm and emission wavelength of 590 nm.
Incubate a mixture of 0.5 μM 7-Ethoxyresorufin, 40 nM of human recombinant CYP1A in TE-enzymatic buffer at 37 °C for 10 min.
Initiate the reaction by adding 0.5 mM NADPH.
Measure the fluorescence at excitation/emission wavelengths 535/590 nm over time.
Remove the medium and add 25 μl of 0.5M sodium hydroxide (NaOH).
Scrape the cells.
Shake the plate for 15 min.
Prepare a calibration curve in the range of 0 to 1200 µg/ml of protein using BSA calibration standard.
Measure the protein.
Dilute stock resazurin solution (1 mg/ml in PBS) in Phenol red-free complete DMEM to 10 µg/ml.
Wash cells once with 100 μl PBS.
Add 100 μl of the resazurin solution to each well.
Incubate for 1 hour at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Measure fluorescence at 535/590 nm (excitation/emission).
Remove resazurin solution if cells are going to be used further.
Add fresh media to wells after removing the resazurin solution.
Wash the cells with PBS.
Add 100 μl of Alamar blue reagent diluted in DMEM medium (1:9 v/v) to each well.
Incubate plates for 2-4 hours, protecting from light.
Measure fluorescence at excitation/emission wavelengths of 530/590 nm or read absorbance at 570 nm with reference wavelength of 600 nm.
Add 10 μl of WST-1 reagents (1:10 final dilution) to each well.
Incubate for 0.5-4 hours, depending on cell density.
Shake thoroughly for 1 min.
Add the same volume of medium and WST-1 as a blank position for ELISA reader.
Measure absorbance at 420 nm with reference wavelength of 690 nm.
Determine resorufin concentrations from their respective calibration standard curves.
Normalize resorufin concentrations to total protein concentration.
Determine protein concentration using a BSA standard curve.
Normalize resorufin concentrations to values obtained from resazurin, Almar blue, or WST-1 assays.
Expose thirty zebrafish larvae in 10 ml Falcon tubes to 7-ethoxyresorufin at a concentration of 8 μM (dissolved in DMSO at 0.1% v/v) for up to 10 hours in triplicate at 28 ± 1°C.
Add dicumarol at a concentration of 10 μM to prevent degradation of resorufin.
After incubation, remove 750 μl of the assay medium and add it to 250 μl of 666-fold diluted β-glucuronidase/arylsulfatase (in 100 mM sodium acetate buffer at pH 4.5) or just buffer only.
Incubate for 2 hours at 37 ± 1°C.
Add 1 ml ethanol to the solution.
Measure fluorescence with an excitation wavelength of 535 nm and emission wavelength of 590 nm.
